content.text:
### View shadcn init CLI options and arguments

Source: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/content/docs/(root)/cli.mdx

Lists the available flags and arguments for the init command, including template selection, component library base, presets, and monorepo configuration.

```bash
Usage: shadcn init [options] [components...]

initialize your project and install dependencies

Arguments:
  components                 names, url or local path to component

Options:
  -t, --template <template>  the template to use. (next, vite, start, react-router, laravel, astro)
  -b, --base <base>          the component library to use. (base, radix, aria)
  -p, --preset [name]        use a preset configuration
  -y, --yes                  skip confirmation prompt. (default: true)
  -d, --defaults             use default configuration: --template=next --preset=nova (default: false)
  -f, --force                force overwrite of existing configuration. (default: false)
  -c, --cwd <cwd>            the working directory. defaults to the current directory.
  -n, --name <name>          the name for the new project.
  -s, --silent               mute output. (default: false)
  --css-variables            use css variables for theming. (default: true)
  --no-css-variables         do not use css variables for theming.
  --monorepo                 scaffold a monorepo project.
  --no-monorepo              skip the monorepo prompt.
  --rtl                      enable RTL support.
  --no-rtl                   disable RTL support.
  --pointer                  enable pointer cursor for buttons.
  --no-pointer               disable pointer cursor for buttons.
  --reinstall                re-install existing UI components.
  --no-reinstall             do not re-install existing UI components.
  -h, --help                 display help for command
```

--------------------------------

### Non-interactive init command flags

Source: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/packages/shadcn/src/commands/init.ts

Flags on the `shadcn init` command that let you scaffold a Vite project non-interactively: `-t/--template vite`, `--monorepo`, `-y/--yes` to skip confirmation prompts, and `-s/--silent` to mute output.

```typescript
.option(
    "-t, --template <template>",
    "the template to use. (next, start, vite, react-router, laravel, astro)"
  )
  .option(
    "-b, --base <base>",
    "the component library to use. (base, radix, aria)"
  )
  .option("--monorepo", "scaffold a monorepo project.")
  .option("--no-monorepo", "skip the monorepo prompt.")
  .option("-p, --preset [name]", "use a preset configuration")
  .option("-y, --yes", "skip confirmation prompt.", true)
```

--------------------------------

### Install chart component using CLI

Source: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/content/docs/components/aria/chart.mdx

Adds the chart component and its dependencies to your project using the shadcn CLI.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add chart
```

--------------------------------

### Install Sidebar via CLI

Source: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/content/docs/components/aria/sidebar.mdx

Use the shadcn CLI to add the sidebar component to your project.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add sidebar
```

--------------------------------

### Scaffold Vite app with preset code using shadcn init

Source: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/skills/shadcn/design-system.md

Initializes a new Vite project using a user-provided preset code. Always include `--no-monorepo` and `-y` to avoid interactive prompts.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest init --preset <code> --template vite --name <app> --no-monorepo -y
```

content.text: Setting up the `@/` path alias that shadcn needs, then initialising shadcn on Radix (same base card.io uses):

input.command:
cd /c/Users/jerem/BioHacks-2026/frontend && python - <<'EOF'
import json
p='tsconfig.json'; t=json.load(open(p))
t['compilerOptions']['baseUrl']='.'
t['compilerOptions']['paths']={'@/*':['./src/*']}
json.dump(t,open(p,'w'),indent=2)
open('vite.config.ts','w').write('''import path from 'node:path'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()],
  resolve: { alias: { '@': path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, './src') } },
})
''')
EOF
npm i -D @types/node@^22 >/dev/null 2>&1; cp src/index.css /tmp/landing-index.css 2>/dev/null; npx shadcn@latest init -b radix -p nova --no-monorepo -y 2>&1 | tail -25

content.text:
The `/home` dashboard is built and Google sign-in now sends people there. I couldn't test an actual sign-in, so the round trip through Google is unverified. The production build passes, and I checked the dashboard in screenshots using a temporary copy of the app with sign-in turned off, so I didn't have to log in.

**One mismatch first:** calhacks doesn't use shadcn; its sidebar and dashboard are hand-built. So, as you asked, it's shadcn components arranged the way calhacks lays out its app. The shadcn setup is the same kind card.io uses: Sidebar, Card, Badge, Avatar, DropdownMenu, Collapsible, ToggleGroup, Table, and Chart for the graphs. Everything uses the landing page's navy and cyan colours, so going from sign-in to the dashboard feels continuous.

**Routes**
- `/` is the landing page. Anyone already signed in goes straight to `/home`.
- `/home` is the dashboard. Signed-out visitors are sent back to `/`.
- Google sign-in returns to `localhost:5173/home`.

**Layout (copied from calhacks)**
- **Sidebar:** a floating panel with a large "Motus" title and a "Start today's assessment" button. Below that are three collapsible groups: Monitoring, Assessments and Clinical. Your Google avatar and a sign-out menu sit at the bottom, and the sidebar can be hidden.
- **Overview page:** a "Monitoring / Overview" label, "Welcome back, {first name}.", and a 30d / 90d / 180d range toggle. Content sits in a 12-column grid with a collapsible session-data table at the bottom.
- **Other nav items:** calhacks-style "Coming soon" pages with a short description of each section.
- **Background:** the landing page's animated grain keeps running behind the dashboard, slower and dimmed.

**What the dashboard shows**
- **Top-line numbers:**
  - A motor function index, where your own baseline is 100.
  - An estimated ALSFRS-R score out of 48 (the standard ALS function rating scale).
  - How fast that score is dropping, in points per month.
  - How many days you completed sessions.
- **ALSFRS-R projection:** the estimated score so far, a 6-month forecast with an uncertainty band, and the scores your clinician gave at visits.
- **Early detection:**
  - How far speech, typing and handwriting each are from your baseline, marked flagged, watch or stable.
  - Your four most-changed features.
  - A chart of each area's drift over time.
- **Alerts:** only for changes that persist across sessions. The card also shows the next clinic visit and a "Share with neurologist" button, which isn't wired up yet.
- **One card per area** comparing baseline to now:
  - **Speech:** speaking rate, pa-ta-ka repetition rate, pause ratio, how long you can hold a note, voice quality.
  - **Typing:** speed, gaps between keys, how long keys are held, how often you correct.
  - **Handwriting:** stroke speed, smoothness, pressure steadiness, accuracy drawing a spiral.

All of these numbers are generated sample data with a visible "Sample data" badge, because nothing captures typing, speech or handwriting yet. They're in `src/lib/sample-data.ts` and need to be swapped for real Supabase queries once data is being stored.

**Supabase settings you still need to change.** The Supabase connection in Claude Code can't edit sign-in settings, so these are dashboard steps:
1. **Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs:** add `http://localhost:5173/home`, plus your production `/home` address later.
2. **Authentication → Sign In / Providers → Google:** turn it on with the client ID and secret, if you haven't already.

**Other changes**
- `src/lib/supabase.ts` now trims the keys in `.env`, so a stray space doesn't count as a key.
- I saw you added the publishable key to `.env`; it's picked up correctly.
- Nothing is committed yet.

content.text:
Your Supabase project is set up correctly. The problem is in Google Cloud: the Google OAuth client doesn't allow your new Supabase project's callback address. Supabase is sending Google this redirect:

```
https://vdnemuejpnoclgnksrvc.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback
```

along with client ID `154772680524-ss1tgqt…apps.googleusercontent.com`. Google rejects it because that callback isn't in the client's list of authorised redirects. If you reused the calhacks Google client, its list only has the calhacks project's callback (`teorfujbhonlpfvfbeia.supabase.co/...`), which is why this one fails.

**Fix it in Google Cloud Console:**
1. Go to **Google Auth Platform → Clients** (console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients) and open the client whose ID starts with `154772680524-ss1tgqt`.
2. Under **Authorised redirect URIs**, add `https://vdnemuejpnoclgnksrvc.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`. Keep any existing entries so calhacks keeps working.
3. Under **Authorised JavaScript origins**, add `http://localhost:5173`.
4. Save. It can take a few minutes to start working.

The redirect URI must match exactly: `https`, no trailing slash, `/auth/v1/callback`.

`localhost:5173/home` does **not** go in Google's list. It belongs in Supabase → **Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs**. If that's missing, you won't get this error; instead, after Google sign-in, Supabase sends you to its default Site URL rather than `/home`.

content.text:
I halved the firing brightness again across the board. The type-check passes, but I haven't screenshotted it this time, so check the live page (Vite will have reloaded it).

| Part of the firing | Before → now |
|---|---|
| Pulse travelling down the axon (glow along the membrane) | about half |
| Glow sprite on that pulse | 0.45 → 0.25 brightness, and smaller (0.4 → 0.3) |
| Cell-body flash | about a third of what it was |
| Membrane brightening after a spike | 0.2 → 0.1 |
| Nucleus flash | 0.5 → 0.25 |
| Axon-terminal flash | 0.7 → 0.35 |
| Particles released at the terminals | 0.7 → 0.4 |
| Magenta signals running up the dendrites | now 60% of before |

The resting neuron and the grey-to-colour effect are unchanged. If it's still too strong, the two biggest settings are `wave * (...)` and `flash * (...)` in the `membraneFS` shader in `src/lib/neuron-sim.ts`.

**GLB (binary glTF)** works best. It's one self-contained file and three.js loads it directly. A **.gltf with its .bin and texture files** also works (card.io's heart is `scene.gltf` + `scene.bin`). If the download is only FBX, OBJ, STL or .blend, send that and I'll convert it to GLB in Blender.

**What helps:**
- **Separate parts:** ideally the cell body, dendrites, axon and terminals are separate, named meshes. Then I can keep the firing effect: signals in along the dendrites, a pulse down the axon, a flash at the terminals. If it's a single merged mesh, I can still estimate each point's distance from the cell body so the pulse travels outward, but it won't be as clean.
- **Size:** under about 10 MB and roughly 200k triangles or fewer, so it stays smooth on a laptop. Draco-compressed GLB is fine.
- **Textures and materials:** optional. I'll replace them with the current grey-to-fluorescent look anyway, the same way card.io recoloured its heart.
- **Animation:** optional. If it has a built-in animation, I can play it the way card.io plays the heartbeat.
- **Licence:** check it allows use in your project, and keep any attribution file with the model, like card.io's `license.txt`.

Drop it in `frontend/public/models/` (e.g. `neuron.glb`) or send me the download link, and I'll swap it in.

content.text:
Your Sketchfab neuron now replaces the generated one on the landing page. It still fires, the build passes, and I checked it in screenshots before and after colouring up and mid-firing.

**How the firing works on a single-mesh model:** the model is one merged mesh with no named parts, so I located them from its shape:
- the cell body is the dense blob at one end;
- the thin straight section is the axon;
- the spray beyond it is the terminals.

From that, the effects map onto the model:
- the pulse travels out along the real axon;
- the faint incoming signals start at the dendrite tips;
- the magenta release dots sit on the actual terminal ends.

It goes from grey to colour with each firing, the same as before.

**Two other changes:**
- **Dark specks fixed:** the released particles and incoming signals were showing as dark spots over the background. This was a long-standing bug in how the glow drew on the transparent canvas, and it also made the old neuron look more solid than intended. Glows now only add light.
- **Incoming signals toned down further:** after that fix they showed as small white dots near the cell body, so I made them dimmer and smaller.

**Licence:** the model is CC BY 4.0, which requires credit. A small credit line now sits at the bottom right of the landing page, and the full attribution is in `public/models/neuron.LICENSE.txt`.

**Files:**
- **Model:** `public/models/neuron.glb`, 288 KB.
- **Mapping code:** `src/lib/model-neuron.ts`. The cell-body centre and axon start are measured constants there, so a different model needs those values re-measured.
- **Fallback:** the generated neuron remains as a fallback if the file fails to load, so the landing page never shows an empty stage.

1	import * as THREE from 'three'
2	import type { NeuronData } from './neuron'
3	
4	/**
5	 * Drives one neuron: incoming synaptic signals run up the dendrites, the soma
6	 * fires, an action potential runs down the axon, and every bouton it reaches
7	 * releases a puff of neurotransmitter.
8	 *
9	 * Colours interpolate from a grey "unstained" state to a fluorescence palette
10	 * as `progress` goes 0 → 1 (the same grey-to-colour arc as card.io's heart).
11	 */
12	
13	const C = (hex: string) => new THREE.Color(hex)
14	const PALETTE = {
15	  membrane: { grey: [C('#4f5663'), C('#a3abb8')], live: [C('#1597bd'), C('#86f2ff')] },
16	  myelin: { grey: [C('#3e434d'), C('#868d99')], live: [C('#3b46b8'), C('#aab4ff')] },
17	  spike: { grey: C('#8f96a3'), live: C('#7fe3f5') },
18	  synapse: { grey: C('#b9bec8'), live: C('#ff4fa3') },
19	  nucleus: { grey: C('#3b3f47'), live: C('#2f4dff') },
20	}
21	
22	const membraneVS = /* glsl */ `
23	attribute float aDist;
24	varying vec3 vN;
25	varying vec3 vV;
26	varying float vDist;
27	void main() {
28	  vec4 mv = modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
29	  vN = normalize(normalMatrix * normal);
30	  vV = normalize(-mv.xyz);
31	  vDist = aDist;
32	  gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mv;
33	}`
34	
35	const membraneFS = /* glsl */ `
36	uniform vec3 uBase;
37	uniform vec3 uRim;
38	uniform vec3 uSpike;
39	uniform vec4 uFronts;
40	uniform float uFlash;
41	uniform float uActivity;
42	uniform float uIntensity;
43	uniform float uFadeRoot;
44	varying vec3 vN;
45	varying vec3 vV;
46	varying float vDist;
47	
48	float front(float f) {
49	  float x = vDist - f;
50	  return exp(-x * x * 2.4);
51	}
52	
53	void main() {
54	  float fres = pow(1.0 - abs(dot(normalize(vN), normalize(vV))), 2.0);
55	  float onAxon = step(0.0, vDist);
56	  float wave = (front(uFronts.x) + front(uFronts.y) + front(uFronts.z) + front(uFronts.w)) * onAxon;
57	  float prox = exp(-abs(min(vDist, 0.0)) * 1.2);
58	  float flash = uFlash * prox;
59	  vec3 col = uBase * (0.16 + 0.5 * fres)
60	           + uRim * fres * 0.5
61	           + uSpike * (wave * (0.05 + 0.1 * fres) + flash * 0.03 * fres);
62	  // Neurites start buried in the soma; fade their open ends so they don't ring.
63	  float root = mix(1.0, smoothstep(0.05, 0.5, abs(vDist)), uFadeRoot);
64	  gl_FragColor = vec4(col * uIntensity * root, 1.0);
65	  #include <colorspace_fragment>
66	  gl_FragColor.a = max(max(gl_FragColor.r, gl_FragColor.g), gl_FragColor.b);
67	}`
68	
69	const particleVS = /* glsl */ `
70	attribute float aLife;
71	attribute float aSize;
72	uniform float uScale;
73	varying float vLife;
74	void main() {
75	  vLife = aLife;
76	  vec4 mv = modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
77	  gl_PointSize = aSize * uScale / -mv.z;
78	  gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mv;
79	}`
80	
81	const particleFS = /* glsl */ `
82	uniform vec3 uColor;
83	uniform sampler2D uMap;
84	varying float vLife;
85	void main() {
86	  float a = texture2D(uMap, gl_PointCoord).a;
87	  gl_FragColor = vec4(uColor * a * vLife, 1.0);
88	  #include <colorspace_fragment>
89	  gl_FragColor.a = max(max(gl_FragColor.r, gl_FragColor.g), gl_FragColor.b);
90	}`
91	
92	export function glowTexture() {
93	  const size = 64
94	  const c = document.createElement('canvas')
95	  c.width = c.height = size
96	  const g = c.getContext('2d')!
97	  const grad = g.createRadialGradient(size / 2, size / 2, 0, size / 2, size / 2, size / 2)
98	  grad.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(255,255,255,1)')
99	  grad.addColorStop(0.18, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.85)')
100	  grad.addColorStop(0.45, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.22)')
101	  grad.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)')
102	  g.fillStyle = grad
103	  g.fillRect(0, 0, size, size)
104	  return new THREE.CanvasTexture(c)
105	}
106	
107	/**
108	 * Light that adds onto a *transparent* canvas: colour and alpha both sum, and
109	 * every source is premultiplied. Plain AdditiveBlending writes alpha ≈ 1, so a
110	 * dim glow becomes an opaque dark speck over the page background.
111	 */
112	const additive = {
113	  transparent: true,
114	  depthWrite: false,
115	  premultipliedAlpha: true,
116	  blending: THREE.CustomBlending,
117	  blendEquation: THREE.AddEquation,
118	  blendSrc: THREE.OneFactor,
119	  blendDst: THREE.OneFactor,
120	  blendSrcAlpha: THREE.OneFactor,
121	  blendDstAlpha: THREE.OneFactor,
122	} as const
123	
124	function membraneMaterial(fadeRoot = 0) {
125	  return new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
126	    vertexShader: membraneVS,
127	    fragmentShader: membraneFS,
128	    uniforms: {
129	      uBase: { value: new THREE.Color() },
130	      uRim: { value: new THREE.Color() },
131	      uSpike: { value: new THREE.Color() },
132	      uFronts: { value: new THREE.Vector4(-1e3, -1e3, -1e3, -1e3) },
133	      uFlash: { value: 0 },
134	      uActivity: { value: 0 },
135	      uIntensity: { value: 1 },
136	      uFadeRoot: { value: fadeRoot },
137	    },
138	    ...additive,
139	  })
140	}
141	
142	type Signal = { sprite: THREE.Sprite; curve: THREE.CatmullRomCurve3 | null; t: number; dur: number }
143

23

33	
34	  // Title + button sit bottom-left (card.io layout), so the cell takes the upper right.

- * Exposes setColors() through `controllerRef` so the page can sweep the
- * palette every frame without remounting WebGL.
-export type GrainController = { setColors: (a: string, b: string, c: string) => void }
-    const renderer = new Renderer({ webgl: 2, alpha: true, antialias: false, dpr: Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2) })
-    const mesh = new Mesh(gl, { geometry: new Triangle(gl), program })
-  }, [controllerRef, timeSpeed, grainAmount, saturation, zoom, contrast, paused])
-import { memo, useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState, type RefObject } from 'react'
-  /** Smoothed 0→1 colour progress, owned by the page. */
-  /** Soma position as viewport fractions, for the ripple. */
-function Scene({ data, progressRef, onSpike, reducedMotion }: Props & { data: NeuronData }) {
-  const neuron = useMemo(() => new NeuronSim(data, { glow, autoInterval: reducedMotion ? 0 : 2.6 }), [data, glow, reducedMotion])
-  /** Drag-to-rotate + wheel zoom state. Plain refs: no re-render per pointer move. */
-  const drag = useRef({ active: false, x: 0, y: 0, moved: 0, yaw: 0, pitch: 0, vYaw: 0, vPitch: 0, zoom: 1 })
-  // Pivot around the middle of the cell, not the soma.
-    for (const geo of [data.soma, data.dendrites, data.axon, data.myelin]) {
-  // Title + button sit bottom-left (card.io layout), so the cell takes the upper right.
-  // Same framing as before: place the cell's centre where the old soma layout put it.
-      // Let a flick coast to a stop.
-            {/* Generous invisible hit target around the soma: click (not drag) to fire. */}
-  // The Sketchfab model; the procedural neuron is the fallback so the stage is never empty.
-        console.warn('Falling back to the procedural neuron:', err)
-      camera={{ position: [0, 0, 20], fov: FOV, near: 0.1, far: 100 }}
-      gl={{ antialias: true, alpha: true, powerPreference: 'high-performance' }}
- * Adapts "Neuron Cell Low-poly Simple" (vitalik.kucha, CC BY 4.0 — see
- * The model is one merged mesh with no part names, so the parts are found
- * geometrically in its own coordinates: long axis = x, soma + dendrites at
- * x < −0.3, a straight axon to x ≈ 1.35, terminals beyond.
-const SOMA = new THREE.Vector3(-1.0, 0.0, 0.2) // densest blob, measured from the vertices
-const SCALE = 3 // match the procedural neuron's scene units
-    if (!source && (o as THREE.Mesh).isMesh) source = (o as THREE.Mesh).geometry
-  if (!source) throw new Error('neuron.glb has no mesh')
-  // Path distance from the soma: dendrites negative, soma 0, axon + terminals positive.
-  const hillockGap = Math.max(0, Math.abs(HILLOCK_X - SOMA.x) - SOMA_R)
-  // Raw-space landmarks, collected before the transform.
-  const raw = Array.from({ length: pos.count }, (_, i) => new THREE.Vector3().fromBufferAttribute(pos, i))
-  for (let x = HILLOCK_X; x <= AXON_END_X; x += 0.15) {
-    const slice = raw.filter((v) => v.x >= x - 0.1 && v.x < x + 0.1)
-    const c = slice.reduce((a, v) => a.add(v), new THREE.Vector3()).divideScalar(slice.length)
-  // Dendrite tips: farthest-point sample of vertices well away from the soma.
-  const dendriteRaw = raw.filter((v) => v.x < HILLOCK_X && v.distanceTo(SOMA) > SOMA_R * 2.2)
-  // Terminal boutons: farthest-point sample of the terminal spray.
